questions.q: What does an in-place MySQL upgrade actually involve?
options: Swapping the server binaries while keeping the same data directory in place
Exporting all data to SQL statements and reloading them into a new server
Migrating to a completely different storage engine
Rewriting the application's connection strings only
questions.explain: An in-place upgrade stops the old mysqld, installs new binaries, and starts them against the same existing data directory.

questions.q: What is the real limitation on in-place upgrades?
options: They're only supported from the immediately preceding GA series to the next one, not multi-version jumps
They can never be automated
They require downtime measured in days
They only work on Windows
questions.explain: A server several major versions behind can't jump straight to the target with a single in-place upgrade; it must step through versions or use dump and reload.

questions.q: What does MySQL Shell's util.checkForServerUpgrade() do?
options: Checks a running server for deprecated features and incompatibilities before an upgrade
Automatically performs the entire upgrade with no further input
Dumps and reloads the database
Configures MySQL Router for the new version
questions.explain: It surfaces problems like deprecated features and reserved keyword collisions before the upgrade is attempted, not after it fails.

questions.q: When is a logical dump and reload the required approach instead of an in-place upgrade?
options: When the version gap is too large for an in-place upgrade, or the target deployment is fundamentally different
Only when the database is smaller than 1 GB
Never — dump and reload is always slower and never necessary
Only for read-only databases
questions.explain: Dump and reload handles version gaps too large for in-place upgrades and moves to different deployments where the data directory can't just be reused.

questions.q: What changed in MySQL's release model starting with MySQL 8.4?
options: Oracle introduced two parallel tracks: fast-moving Innovation releases and stable Long Term Support (LTS) releases
MySQL stopped releasing new versions entirely
All releases became LTS by default
In-place upgrades were discontinued in favor of dump and reload only
questions.explain: MySQL 8.4 was the first LTS release under the new model, giving production systems a stable track distinct from the faster Innovation releases.
